# Weed-removal robot electrical power design

This illustrated record consolidates the six technical questions in this thread. The figures show current paths and component arrangements. Numerical examples illustrate the calculations. Final settings depend on the selected battery, panel, motor, and driver.

## 1. How much energy does MPPT recover?

Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) holds the panel near the voltage and current that produce its maximum available power. A DC–DC stage converts that power to the battery bus voltage. A conventional PWM solar charger connects the panel to the battery during its on-time, pulling the panel operating voltage close to battery voltage. The panel's rated sunlight-to-electricity efficiency stays the same. The power harvested and delivered to the battery terminals changes.

![Solar charger comparison at a 13 V battery bus](data:image/png;base64,)

*Solar charger comparison at a 13 V battery bus.*

| Example operating point | Conventional PWM | MPPT |
|---|---:|---:|
| Panel operating voltage | 13.5 V | 18 V |
| Panel current | 6.0 A | 5.56 A |
| Power drawn from panel | 81 W | 100 W |
| Power delivered to a 13 V battery bus | 78 W | 97 W |
| Energy delivered in one hour at these conditions | 78 Wh | 97 Wh |

The example uses Victron's 100 W panel and PWM operating point. The PWM output is 13 V × 6 A. The MPPT output assumes 97% converter efficiency and operation at the maximum power point. The resulting gain is 19 W, or about **24% more battery-terminal power relative to PWM**. The battery's own losses determine how much energy it stores.

Higher panel temperature generally lowers maximum-power voltage and may narrow the advantage. A full battery, low-light conversion losses, shading, and available load affect actual energy harvest. Estimate runtime from watt-hours delivered over representative field conditions.

[Victron PWM versus MPPT technical paper](https://www.victronenergy.com/upload/documents/White-paper-Which-solar-charge-controller-PWM-or-MPPT.pdf) · [Morningstar controller FAQ](https://www.morningstarcorp.com/faq/)

## 2. Can I buy an MPPT module off the shelf?

Yes. Ready-to-wire chargers are available for drive batteries, and compact boards serve lower-power auxiliary batteries. These are the example prices quoted in the discussion, in USD.

| Product | Quoted price | Application |
|---|---:|---|
| [Victron SmartSolar 75/15](https://shopsolarkits.com/products/victron-energy-smartsolar-mppt-75v-15-amp-12-24-volt-solar-charge-controller-bluetooth) | $67.15 | Step-down charger for 12 V or 24 V batteries, 15 A maximum charging current, 75 V maximum PV open-circuit voltage, and 220 W or 440 W nominal PV power on 12 V or 24 V systems respectively. |
| [Genasun GVB-8 Boost](https://sunforgellc.com/product/gvb-8/) | $180 | Step-up option when the panel operating voltage is below the required battery voltage. The quoted 8S LiFePO₄ model charges to 28.4 V. |
| [Waveshare Solar Power Manager](https://www.waveshare.com/product/modules/solar-power-manager.htm) | $8.99 | Small board for a single 3.7 V lithium cell. The 6–24 V figure describes the solar panel input. |
| [Analog Devices LT8490 DC2069A](https://www.analog.com/en/resources/evaluation-hardware-and-software/evaluation-boards-kits/dc2069a.html) | — | Buck-boost evaluation board with schematic and design files. The demo board is configured for a 12 V sealed lead-acid battery. |

Choose a buck charger when hot-panel operating voltage stays above the full-charge voltage by the controller's required margin. Choose boost when the panel operates below the required charge voltage and the panel falls within the boost model's input limits. Consider buck-boost when operating voltage can cross the battery voltage. Check cold-weather panel open-circuit voltage, maximum PV input current, and the battery's chemistry, charging voltage and current limits.

[Victron SmartSolar technical specifications](https://www.victronenergy.com/media/pg/Manual_SmartSolar_MPPT_75-10_up_to_100-20/en/technical-specifications.html)

## 3. What happens when the robot runs while solar charging is active?

On a shared DC bus the battery sees **net current**. With positive current defined as charging, battery current equals charger output current minus total load current, ignoring other sources. Solar power can flow directly to the motor driver and electronics.

![Shared DC bus with bidirectional battery current](data:image/png;base64,)

*Shared DC bus with bidirectional battery current.*

| MPPT output | Robot bus load | Battery current |
|---:|---:|---|
| 8 A | 20 A | 12 A discharge |
| 8 A | 8 A | Approximately zero |
| 8 A available | 3 A | Up to 5 A charge, within the battery's limits |

Lower battery current reduces voltage sag and resistive heating. At unchanged internal resistance, 12 A produces about 36% of the resistive heating at 20 A. Solar can also reduce the depth of discharge for a given job. Victron's Lithium Smart example lists 2,500 cycles at 80% depth of discharge and 5,000 at 50%, to an endpoint of 80% remaining nominal capacity. Those figures apply to that product line.

This operating arrangement is acceptable with a compatible charger and BMS. Size the drive battery and wiring for peak demand with zero solar contribution. When the motors stop, the battery may receive the full available charger output. If the charging profile ends on a tail-current threshold, verify whether the charger measures actual battery current. A parallel load can keep charger output current above the threshold. A supported battery shunt or a separate power path can resolve that measurement issue.

[TI battery charger and power-path designs](https://www.ti.com/lit/an/slua376/slua376.pdf) · [Victron Lithium Smart technical data](https://www.victronenergy.com/media/pg/Lithium_Battery_Smart/en/technical-data.html) · [Victron Current Sense explanation](https://www.victronenergy.com/upload/documents/Blue_Smart_IP22_Charger_230V_manual/181363-Blue_Smart_Charger-pdf-en.pdf)

## 4. Which BMS settings depend on battery type?

| BMS function | Settings to derive from the cell and pack specifications |
|---|---|
| Cell voltage protection | Overvoltage and undervoltage thresholds for each series cell group, trip delays, and recovery thresholds. One group can reach a limit before the total pack voltage does. |
| Current protection | Separate charge and discharge limits, allowable peak durations, and fast short-circuit protection. Check parallel cell count, the BMS, and the pack connections. |
| Temperature protection | Separate charging and discharging temperature limits, plus derating if supported. Use battery temperature. |
| Cell balancing | Minimum voltage for balancing and the cell-voltage differences that start and stop it. |
| Fault recovery | Voltage, temperature, and timing conditions for reconnecting after a fault. |

The MPPT charger applies the normal charging profile. Set its voltage, current, termination and any absorption or float stages to the pack maker's requirements. The BMS enforces protection limits. A compatible BMS can also command the charger to stop or reduce current. Set the robot's normal low-battery slowdown or shutdown to act before the BMS undervoltage trip.

| Example | Charging profile or limit |
|---|---|
| Victron 25.6 V Lithium Smart LiFePO₄ | 28.4 V recommended charge voltage and +5 to +50 °C charge range. |
| Seven Molicel P42A cells in series | 4.20 V per cell gives 29.4 V for 7S. The cell datasheet specifies constant-current/constant-voltage charging and 0 to +45 °C. The assembled pack can impose tighter limits. |
| Trojan deep-cycle AGM | Apply the specified absorption and float stages with temperature compensation. Trojan's deep-cycle AGM guide excludes equalization. |

[TI BQ76952 technical reference manual](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/sluuby2b/sluuby2b.pdf) · [Victron Lithium Smart manual](https://www.victronenergy.com/media/pg/Lithium_Battery_Smart/en/technical-data.html) · [Molicel P42A datasheet](https://www.molicel.com/wp-content/uploads/INR21700P42A-V4-80092.pdf) · [Trojan AGM guide](https://assets.ctfassets.net/nh2mdhlonj7m/2o9A7l6uYgA54vsDwTDpsM/dbc147d069263a1bed39c92594274aef/Trojan_QSG_AGM.pdf)

## 5. Which motors drive agricultural robot wheels?

Geared three-phase brushless DC motors are common in documented battery-powered agricultural robot designs. A sealed, sensored BLDC gearmotor with an encoder is a starting point for an independently driven wheel that must creep smoothly between crops. Match the motor, feedback and controller. BLDC and PMSM are closely related permanent-magnet motor designs. Check the motor's commutation and feedback requirements when choosing a driver.

![Separate reduction drive and geared hub motor layouts](data:image/png;base64,)

*Separate reduction drive and geared hub motor layouts.*

| Drive layout | Documented example | Design consideration |
|---|---|---|
| BLDC with a separate reduction stage | Thorvald II uses a 500 W BLDC motor, timing belt, in-wheel planetary gearbox, Hall sensors and an encoder. | Separate components give flexibility in mounting and ratio selection. |
| Geared BLDC hub motor | The Amiga used in a mechanical weeding study has four sealed 250–500 W geared BLDC hubs. | Compact arrangement. Check sealing and allowable radial and axial wheel loads. |
| Brushed DC gearmotor | A published agricultural research robot uses four 12 V brushed motors with 131.25:1 metal gearboxes. | A simple prototype option. A reversible H-bridge can drive the motor, and brushes wear over time. |

Size the drive from wheel torque and speed. Use loaded mass, wheel radius, maximum slope, rolling resistance, tool drag and turning demand. Check continuous torque at working speed and peak torque during starts and turns. A 400 mm wheel at 0.5 m/s turns at about 23.9 rpm. A 3,000 rpm motor would need about 126:1 reduction to reach that speed at 3,000 rpm. That calculation sets the speed ratio. The torque, gearbox efficiency, traction, and duty cycle determine whether it can do the work.

[Thorvald II drivetrain](https://www.mdpi.com/2218-6581/6/4/24) · [Amiga mechanical weeding study](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11119-026-10445-3) · [Brushed research drivetrain](https://www.osti.gov/pages/servlets/purl/1799040) · [Microchip commutation reference](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/UserGuides/MCP8027-QFN40-BLDC-Motor-Drive-EVB-User-Guide-DS50003682.pdf)

## 6. Why and how should the BMS handle charging and discharging pulses?

A motor-start surge can be acceptable for a specified duration. Sustained high current can overheat the current path or cause a weak cell to hit undervoltage. A short circuit requires a much faster response. Regenerative braking can send current back toward the battery. If the battery is full, cold, or disconnected by protection, regenerative energy can raise DC bus voltage.

![BMS response to discharge surges and short circuits](data:image/png;base64,)

*BMS response to discharge surges and short circuits.*

| Event | Control and protection |
|---|---|
| Motor start or stall | Use the motor driver's acceleration ramp and current limits during normal operation. Coordinate the BMS overcurrent threshold and delay with verified pack pulse limits. |
| Short circuit | Use independent fast hardware protection and an appropriately rated DC pack fuse. Coordinate clearing time and DC interrupt rating with the available fault current. |
| Capacitor inrush at power-up | Use a current-limited precharge path for the motor driver's DC bus capacitors, then close the main path once the voltage difference is within the design limit. TI calls this load-side feature *predischarge*. |
| Solar charging | The MPPT converter controls normal charge current and voltage. The BMS can block charging for cell overvoltage, charge overcurrent, or temperature violations. |
| Regenerative braking | Limit regen using the battery's allowed charge current, accounting for solar contribution and other loads. If the pack cannot accept the energy, use a driver-supported brake resistor or another suitable braking method. |

A bidirectional shunt lets the BMS distinguish charge and discharge. Configure separate thresholds and delays for charge overcurrent, discharge overcurrent, and short circuits. Normal high-frequency PWM belongs to the charger and motor driver. The BMS charge and discharge switches act as protective disconnects in this architecture.

Measure **battery-side current** during startup, tight turns and heavy tool loading with no solar contribution. BLDC phase current is a separate measurement. If regen is enabled, capture battery current and bus voltage during braking with solar active. Use the measured duration and repetition of the peaks, the pack's allowed current-versus-time limits, and the ratings of the BMS, wiring, and connectors when setting the protection.

[TI BQ76952 technical reference manual](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/sluuby2b/sluuby2b.pdf) · [TI solar charger example](https://www.ti.com/product/BQ24650) · [ODrive DC bus and braking configuration](https://github.com/odriverobotics/ODrive/blob/master/Firmware/odrive-interface.yaml)
